items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Module docstring and parse_tag/rebuild_tag docstrings help, but the tokenizer logic is full of single-letter names (s, i, j, k, n, e, q, v, c, c2, r, r2), e.g. `q = s[k]` and `e = s.find(q, k + 1)`. Cap applies: at most accept.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: `sanitize()` is one function of roughly 115 lines, with comment, bogus-comment, end-tag, start-tag and raw-text handling all inline and nested 4+ levels deep. The cap for a function over 100 lines applies. The policy constants and helpers are separated well.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Files are opened with `with`, `surrogateescape` keeps bytes intact, and there is a usage check on argv. File I/O has no error handling. The fixpoint loop in `filter_html` has no iteration limit. The `_ctrl` range and the fixed scheme lists are magic constants.

items.name: Obfuscated vectors neutralised
items.evidence: General rules throughout: case-insensitive on* names, `_norm` (html.unescape plus control-character stripping) applied to every attribute, data: allowlist, srcdoc denied, xlink:href covered, script/iframe/object/embed denied, CSS unescaping, and repeated passes until stable defeat split <scr<script>ipt>. Chromium check: 0 alerts after filtering.

items.name: Minimal edits on dirty documents
items.name_zh: 含恶意内容的文档仅做最小修改
items.evidence: Edits are byte-precise and keep quoting and whitespace, but some removals are too broad: an entire <style> block is dropped for one bad token, any attribute value containing 'javascript:' is dropped (title text included), and http iframes are removed.
